Rashi on Nazir 34b:10:1.hebrew: עד שיפרוט לך הכתוב - שלא תהא מרבה אלא כעין הפרט, כדרך שפרט לך בנזיר, שלאחר שכתב את הכלל, בא וכתב לך פרט: "מחרצנים ועד זג". ור"א סבר כר"א בן עזריה, דמוקים ליה להאי "מחרצנים ועד זג" — עד שיאכל שני חרצנים וזג:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:10:1.english: Until the verse specifies for you - That you include only that which is similar to the detail, in the manner that it specified for you with regard to the nazirite, that after it wrote the generalization, it came and wrote for you a detail: “From pits to grape skin.” And Rabbi Eliezer holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, who establishes this [verse], “From pits to grape skin,” [to mean] until he eats two pits and a grape skin.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:12:1.english: Guharkei - Small grapes that grow among the other, large berries.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:12:2.english: Invei decharin - Grapes that have become wormy.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:12:3.hebrew: בין הבינים - אותו דבר הקרוש שבין הזג והחרצן, שממנו נעשין שמרים:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:12:3.english: In between - That congealed substance between the skin and the seed, from which dregs are made.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:1:1.hebrew: במשנה ראשונה - היו שונין שאינו חייב עד שישתה רביעית יין. בא ר"ע ואמר: אפי' שרה פיתו ביין, ויש יין מובלע בתוך הפת כדי זית — חייב:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:1:1.english: In the initial Mishnah - They used to teach that he is not liable until he drinks a quarter-log of wine. Rabbi Akiva came and said: Even if he soaked his bread in wine, and there is wine absorbed within the bread equal to an olive-bulk, he is liable.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:3:1.hebrew: עלין ולולבין - של גפן במשמע הכתוב, שאמר: "מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין". לולבין — אלו חוטין רכין שבגפן:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:3:1.english: Leaves and tendrils - [Those] of the vine are implied by the verse, which states: “From anything that is made of the grapevine” [Numbers 6:4]. Tendrils — these are the tender shoots on the vine.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:5:1.hebrew: מיין ושכר יזיר מיעט - יין הראוי להשתכר בו אסור לו, אבל מידי אחרינא לא:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:5:1.english: “He shall abstain from wine and strong drink” restricts - Wine that is fit to become intoxicated with is forbidden to him, but anything else [is] not.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:6:1.english: All matters - And even leaves and shoots.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:6:2.english: Branches - Vine branches, as we translate “sarigim” [as] “shivshin” (Genesis 40).

Rashi on Nazir 34b:7:1.english: Just as the detail is explicitly fruit and fruit waste - Such as grapes, wine, and vinegar.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:7:2.hebrew: אף כל פרי ופסולת - להביא גוהרקי ועינבין דיכרין, כדלקמן בסמוך:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:7:2.english: So too, everything [is] fruit and [fruit] waste - [This serves] to include guharki [underdeveloped grapes] and invei dikhrin [worm-eaten grapes], as [stated] shortly below.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:8:1.hebrew: אף כל פרי גמור - ולא דבר אחר, ולא גוהרקי, ולא עינבין דיכרין:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:8:1.english: So too, everything [must be] a complete fruit - And not anything else, nor guharki [unripe grapes], nor invin dikhrin [wormy grapes].

Rashi on Nazir 34b:8:2.english: If so - That only a complete fruit is to be included in it.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:8:3.hebrew: מה הניח לך הכתוב במשמעו שלא אמר - שתהא למד מן הפרט? אם ענבים לחים ויבשים — הא כתיב, כו':
Rashi on Nazir 34b:8:3.english: What has the verse left you in its meaning that it has not stated - That you should derive [it] from the detail? If [you say] fresh and dried grapes — behold, it is [already] written, etc.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:8:4.hebrew: אלא כלשון הראשון - ״אף כל פרי ופסולת פרי״, שאם אתה אומר ״אף כל פרי גמור״ — נמצא דאינו מרבה שום דבר בעולם:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:8:4.english: Rather, in accordance with the first version - [Which states:] “So too, everything [must be] fruit and fruit refuse.” For if you say, “So too, everything [must be] a complete fruit,” it turns out that [the generalization] does not include anything in the world.

Rashi on Nazir 34b:9:1.hebrew: ומאחר שסופינו לרבות כל דבר - יין וחומץ (ענבים לחים ויבשים), ומרבה יין גוהרקי ועינבין דיכרין מאף כל; והיינו דהניח הכתוב במשמעו שלא אמר (וענבים לחים ויבשים):
Rashi on Nazir 34b:9:1.english: And since we ultimately include everything - [In addition to] wine and vinegar (moist and dry grapes), [the generalization] includes wine of unripe grapes [guharki] and wormy grapes [einavin dikhrin] from “so too, everything”; and that is what the verse left in its implied meaning that it did not state [explicitly] (and moist and dry grapes).

Rashi on Nazir 34b:9:2.hebrew: מה ת"ל - פרט האחרון, דכתיב: ״מחרצנים ועד זג לא יאכל״ — אי משום דרבי אלעזר בן עזריה, ליכתביה לגבי פרטי; בתר כללא למה לי:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:9:2.english: What is the meaning when the verse states - [With regard to] the final detail, as it is written: “From pits to grape skin he shall not eat” — if [it is needed] on account of [the teaching] of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, let [the verse] write it alongside the [first] details; why do I need [it written] after the generalization?

Rashi on Nazir 34b:9:3.hebrew: אלא לומר לך כל מקום שאתה מוצא - בכל התורה שיהא שם פרט וכלל בלבד, אי אתה רשאי למושכו ולדונו כעין הפרט, אלא שהכלל נעשה מוסף על הפרט, ואיתרבו להו כל מילי:
Rashi on Nazir 34b:9:3.english: Rather, to tell you, wherever you find - In the entire Torah where there is only a detail and a generalization, you are not permitted to draw it [the generalization] and interpret it like the detail; rather, the generalization is made an addition to the detail, and everything is included.

Rashi on Sukkah 6a:3:2.hebrew: כדי רביעית יין - בשאר איסורי נזיר, דאיכא למאן דאמר במסכת נזיר (דף לד:) דחרצנים ולולבין ועליו מצטרפין לשיעור רביעית יין, שאם יתנם לכוס מלא יין עד שיצא ממנו רביעית יין. ואין דומה המשער בכוס מלא מים למשער ביין, משום דיין עב הוא ואינו ממהר לצאת, אלא נברץ ונגדש על שפת הכוס יותר מן המים:
Rashi on Sukkah 6a:3:2.english: The quantity of a quarter-log of wine - [This measure applies] to the other forbidden [products] of a nazirite, for there is one who says in tractate Nazir (daf 34b) that grape pits, tendrils, and its leaves combine to the measure of a quarter-log of wine, such that if one places them into a cup full of wine until a quarter-log of wine overflows from it [that is the liable quantity]. And one who measures [displacement] in a cup full of water is not comparable to one who measures in wine, because wine is thick and does not quickly spill out, but rather mounds up and heaps over the brim of the cup more than water [does].

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:12:1.hebrew: גוהרקי - פי': בוסר. וחבירו בפ' כל שעה (פסחים ד' כה:): "הוה שייף לברתיה בגוהרקי דערלה":
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:12:1.english: Guharkei - Explanation: unripe fruit. And its counterpart [appears] in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 25b): "[Ravina] was rubbing his daughter with unripe fruit of orlah."

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:12:2.english: Einavin dikhrin - Grapes that have become wormy.

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:12:3.hebrew: [דבין הבינים] - דהיינו גוף הענב. והכי משמע לישנא דקרא: "מחרצנים ועד זג" — פירוש: מה שבין חרצן לזג. וקשה: דההיא גוף הענב, וכבר כתב "ענבים"! לכן פר"ת: דהיינו ענבים קטנים שבין הגדולים, שאינם רואין פני החמה ואינם מתבשלין כל כך, ולא יהיו גדולים לעולם. וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך "ועד" לבין הביניים? והלא כבר מרבינן אפי' בוסר מכעין הפרט! ושמא י"ל: דה"נ גריעי מבוסר, לפי שבוסר יבא לכלל ענבים גדולים. ועוד י"ל: דאי לאו "ועד" מרבין בין הביניים, הוו מרבים מכעין הפרט בין הביניים ולא בוסר. ועוד יש לקיים פירוש ראשון, והכי פירושו: אם ליקט האוכל שבין החרצן כדי כזית ואכלו — לוקה, ולא אמרי' דבטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם; והא לא שמעינן ליה מ"ענבים" דקרא:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:12:3.english: [That which is in between] - That is, the body [i.e., the flesh] of the grape. And so implies the wording of the verse: "from pits to grape skin" (Numbers 6:4) — meaning, that which is between the pit and the skin. And this is difficult: For that is the body of the grape, and [the Torah] already wrote "grapes" (Numbers 6:3)! Therefore, R. Tam explained that this refers to small grapes that are between the large ones, which do not see the face of the sun and do not ripen so much, and will never become large. And if you say: Why was "and up to" [ve'ad] needed for [the grapes] in between? Behold, we already include even unripe grapes from "similar to the specific"! And perhaps it can be said that these are inferior to unripe grapes, since unripe grapes will eventually reach the stage of large grapes. And furthermore, it can be said that if not for "and up to" including [the grapes] in between, they would have included from "similar to the specific" [the grapes] in between, and not unripe grapes. And furthermore, the first explanation can be maintained, and this is its meaning: If one collected the edible portion that is between the pits to the amount of an olive-bulk and ate it, he is flogged, and we do not say that his view is nullified by that of all people; and this we would not have learned from "grapes" in the verse.

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:13:1.hebrew: מחרצנים ועד זג ל"ל - וא"ת: והא שפיר איצטריך, דאפי' חרצנים וזג אסר רחמנא, דאע"פ שאינן ראויין לאכילה; וגם איצטריכו למלקות, כדאמר לקמן (נזיר ד' לח:): "אכל חרצן — לוקה שתים, זג — לוקה שתים"? (ויש לומר): דהכי קאמר: ל"ל? לכתביה מקמיה! וקשה: דהיאך סבור דלא יאמר "נעשה כלל מוסיף על הפרט"? לכך נראה, דה"ק: לכתוב "חרצן וזג":
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:13:1.english: "From pits to grape skin," why do I need [it]? - And if you say: But surely it is well needed, for the Merciful One forbade even pits and grape skin even though they are not fit for eating, and they were also needed for lashes, as [the Gemara] says later (Nazir 38b): "[If] he ate a pit, he is lashed twice; [if he ate] a grape skin, he is lashed twice"? (And one can say) that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: Why do I need [it written here]? Let [Scripture] write it before it! But this is difficult: For how could [the Gemara] suppose that it would not say "the generalization becomes added to the detail"? Therefore, it appears that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: Let [Scripture] write [simply] "a pit and a grape skin."

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:1:1.hebrew: וחייב על היין בפני עצמו ועל הענבים בפני עצמן ועל הזגין בפני עצמן - ונראה דעיקר חידוש לת"ק בא לומר: חייב על הזגין בפני עצמן אם אכל לבד מן הזגין. ואההיא אתא לאפלוגי ר"א בן עזריה, ואומר דאינו חייב עד שיאכל שני חרצנים וזג — [דחרצנים הם] הגרעינין בענבין וזגין הם הקליפה שלהן, ומרבה חרצנים בלשון רבים וזג בלשון יחיד, כדמפרש הש"ס. ור"א סבר כר' יוסי, דאמר: חרצנים אלו הגרעינים:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:1:1.english: "And he is liable for the wine by itself, and for the grapes by themselves, and for the skins by themselves" - And it appears that the primary novelty of the first tanna is to say that he is liable for the skins by themselves if he ate only from the skins. And it is on that [point] that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya came to disagree, and he says that he is not liable until he eats two seeds and a skin — [for ḥartzannim are] the seeds in grapes and zaggim are their skin, and [the verse] mentions ḥartzannim in the plural and zag in the singular, as the Gemara explains. And Rabbi Elazar holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who said: "Ḥartzannim are the seeds."

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:2:1.hebrew: [החרצנים אלו החיצונים] - קליפה שבחוץ, [והזגין אלו הם] מבפנים. "ר' יוסי אומר" — ולאפלוגי הוא דאתא, ופירש המקרא להיפך: אלו הקליפה החיצונה. וסימן שלא תטעה: כזוג של בהמה — החיצון נקרא זוג; כן בענבים, החיצון נקרא זוג:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:2:1.english: ["The ḥartzannim are the outer ones"] - [This refers to] the peel that is on the outside, [and the zaggim are those] from the inside. [As for the statement,] "Rabbi Yosei says" — he came to disagree [with Rabbi Yehuda], and he explained the verse in the opposite way: these are the outer peel. And a mnemonic so that you will not err: Like the bell of an animal, [where] the outer part is called a zog; so too with grapes, the outer part is called a zog.

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:3:1.hebrew: גפן עצמו לא - כגון עלין ולולבין, מדלא תנא [רבותא] גפן עצמו:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:3:1.english: The vine itself, no - Such as leaves and tendrils, since [the Tanna] did not teach [the novelty of] "the vine itself."

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:3:2.hebrew: אפי' עלין ולולבין במשמע - כדדרשינן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:3:2.english: "Even leaves and tendrils are included" - As [the Gemara] expounds nearby.

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:4:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי אסיפא - אבל אדיוקא דרישא לא, דמשמע שפיר בלישנא דהיוצא מן הגפן אפי' עלין ולולבין:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:4:1.english: Some say [this] with regard to the latter clause - But [they do] not [apply it] to the inference of the first clause, as the phrasing "that which emerges from the vine" well implies even leaves and tendrils.

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:5:1.hebrew: מיין ושכר יזיר מיעט - אע"ג דדרשי' לי' בפ"ק (לעיל נזיר ד.) לאסור יין [של מצוה כיין של רשות], ושכר לילפי למקדש — מ"מ איכא מיעוטין טובא, דכתיב: "מיין ושכר יזיר", "חומץ יין וחומץ שכר לא ישתה", "וענבים לחים ויבשים לא יאכל". "מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין" — ריבה. אבל "מחרצנים ועד זג" לא דריש ליה למעוטי כרבנן, דאיצטריך ליה לכדר' אלעזר בן עזריה דבסמוך, דאינו חייב עד שיאכל שני חרצנים וזג:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:5:1.english: "He shall abstain from wine and strong drink" restricts - Even though we expounded it in the first chapter (above, Nazir 4a) to forbid wine [of a mitzvah like wine of optional permission], and "strong drink" to derive [the law] for the Sanctuary, nevertheless there are many restrictions, as it is written: "He shall abstain from wine and strong drink," "he shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of strong drink," "neither shall he eat fresh grapes or dried." "Anything that is made of the grapevine" amplifies. However, "from pits to grape skin" he does not expound to restrict like the Rabbis [who expound it as a detail], because he requires it for that of Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah nearby: that he is not liable until he eats two pits and a grape skin.

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:6:1.hebrew: מאי ריבה ריבה כל מילי ואפי' עלין ולולבין ומאי מיעט שבישתא - זמורה, כדמתרגמינן: "שלשה שריגים" — "תלתא שיבשין":
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:6:1.english: “What does it amplify? It amplifies all matters,” and even leaves and tendrils; “and what does it restrict? It restricts branches” - [This means] a vine branch, as we translate [in the Targum]: “Three branches” [Genesis 40:10] — “telata shivshin.”

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:7:1.hebrew: מיין ושכר יזיר פרט - מדה זו ניתנה לידרש כעין כלל ופרט וכלל, ויש חילוק קצת בין המדות, כדכתב בסוף הסוגיא:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:7:1.english: "He shall abstain from wine and strong drink" — a detail - This [hermeneutic] rule was given to be expounded similar to a generalization, a detail, and a generalization [kelal u-ferat u-khelal], and there is a slight difference between the rules, as [the Gemara] writes at the end of the sugya.

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:7:2.hebrew: מה פרט מפורש בנזיר ענבים פרי אף (על) כל פרי - מפרש בסמוך: לאיתויי בוסר, ופסולת פרי — ענבים שהתליעו, ולמעט עלין ולולבין, שאינו כעין הפרט. "אי: מה פרט מפורש פרי גמור אף כל פרי גמור" — יש מפרשין דהכי פירושו: ונמעט גם בוסר, גם ענבים שהתליעו. ולא נראה: חדא, דחומץ כתיב דהוי פסולת פרי, ומאי שנא ענבים שהתליעו מחומץ? וע"ק, דאם נמעט תרווייהו, מה אנו מרויחין בכלל ופרט מה שלא נכתב בפירוש? וגם לשון "פרי גמור" משמע דאתי למעוטי פרי שאינו גמור, כמו בוסר. לכן נראה למורי דה"פ: "אף כל פרי גמור" — ולאפוקי בוסר, אבל ענבים שהתליעו נרבה כעין הפרט. ומשני: "א"כ מה הניח לך שלא אמרו? ענבים לחים ויבשים הא כתיבי, יין וחומץ [הא כתיבי], הא אין עליך לדון כלשון אחרון אלא כלשון ראשון". פי': אם כן דנמעט בוסר, נמצא השאר מפורש, ומה נרויח שאנו דורשין פרט וכלל ופרט? ואם תאמר: והא איכא ענבים שהתליעו שלא נכתבו! ויש לומר: דתרי פרטי כתיבי: פרי, דהיינו ענבים, ופסולת פרי, דהיינו חומץ; ואין לך לרבויי מכל פרט כעין הפרט? ולכך יש עליך לדון ולרבות גם בוסר מפרט ענבים, גם ענבים שהתליעו מפרט דחומץ, ולמעוטי עלין ולולבין שאינו כעין הפרט:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:7:2.english: “Just as the detail specified regarding a nazirite, grapes, is fruit, so too, any fruit” - [The Gemara] explains nearby [below, that this comes] to include unripe grapes, and [as for] “fruit waste,” [it comes to include] grapes that became worm-infested, and to exclude leaves and tendrils, which are not similar to the detail. [Regarding the challenge:] “If [you suggest]: Just as the detail is clearly defined as a fully formed fruit, so too, everything [forbidden] must be a fully formed fruit” — some explain that this is its meaning: and let us exclude both unripe grapes and grapes that became worm-infested. But this does not appear [correct]: First, for vinegar is written [in the verse], which is fruit waste; and how are grapes that became worm-infested any different from vinegar? And furthermore, it is difficult: for if we exclude both of them, what do we gain through [the exegesis of] a generalization and a detail that was not explicitly written [in the verses]? And also, the phrasing “a fully formed fruit” implies that it comes to exclude fruit that is not fully formed, such as unripe grapes. Therefore, it appears to my teacher that this is its explanation: “So too, everything must be a fully formed fruit” — and [this is] to exclude unripe grapes; but grapes that became worm-infested we should include [as being] similar to the detail [of vinegar]. And [the Gemara] answers: “If so, what has [the verse] left for you that it did not state? Fresh and dried grapes are written! Wine and vinegar [are written]! Thus, you cannot learn in accordance with the latter version, but rather in accordance with the first version.” Explanation: If so, that we exclude unripe grapes, the rest is found to be explicitly stated [in the Torah], and what would we gain by expounding [via] a detail, a generalization, and a detail? And if you say: But isn't there [still] grapes that became worm-infested, which were not written [and which would be included]? One can say: Two details are written: fruit, that is, grapes, and fruit waste, that is, vinegar. And must you not include from each detail that which is similar to that detail? And therefore you must deduce and include both unripe grapes from the detail of grapes and grapes that became worm-infested from the detail of vinegar, and exclude leaves and tendrils, which are not similar to the detail.

Tosafot on Nazir 34b:9:1.hebrew: ומאחר שסופינו לרבות כל דבר מה תלמוד לומר מחרצנים ועד זג - ואם תאמר: והא איצטריך לפרט אחרון? י"ל דהכי פירושו: לכתוב ליה קודם הכלל. ומשני: לומר לך כל מקום שאתה מוצא פרט וכלל — פירוש: בעלמא, וכן הכא גבי נזיר: לולא לא נכתב חרצן וזג שהוא פרט אחרון, אי אתה רשאי לדונו ולישבו כעין הפרט, אלא נעשה כלל מוסף על הפרט — והיינו מרבינן עלין ולולבין נמי — עד שיפרוט לך הכתוב פרט אחר הכלל כדרך שפרט לך בנזיר:
Tosafot on Nazir 34b:9:1.english: "And as we eventually include everything, what is the meaning when the verse states: 'From pits to grape skin'?" - And if you say: But wasn't [this phrase] needed as a final detail? One can say that this is the meaning [of the question]: Let [Scripture] write it before the generalization. And [the Gemara] answers: [This serves] to tell you that wherever you find a detail and a generalization — the explanation being: in general [throughout the Torah], and so too here regarding a nazirite, had "pits" and "grape skin," which is the final detail, not been written, you would not be permitted to evaluate it and establish it like the detail; rather, the generalization would become added to the detail — and we would include leaves and tendrils as well — until Scripture specifies a detail after the generalization, in the manner that it specified for you in [the case of] the nazirite.
